stories.headline: Kharge claims stage 'purified' after his speech in Haldwani, govt promises action
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Leader of the opposition in Rajya Sabha and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge alleged in RS Thursday people associated with BJP "purified" the stage at Ramlila Maidan in Haldwani, two days after he made a speech there on Aug 8.
Leader of the House J P Nadda said BJP did not support such activities, the incident was "painful" and action would be taken against the culprits.
Raising the issue during zero hour, Kharge said, "I did not mention the name of any caste or religion, I only spoke about the problems of the people. But with great pain, I have to say that after my speech, BJP people performed a 'havan' (ritual) there and carried out purification of the stage. Is this the way democracy works? How are you protecting the Constitution?"
Kharge demanded that cases be registered under Untouchability Act and those involved be arrested.
Nadda said the issue shouldn't be politicised or sensationalised. "There will be a detailed investigation. Let me make it clear that BJP never subscribes to such activities. I condemn this. The incident has hurt your (Kharge) sentiments and it is a matter of regret for all of us," he said.
Some MPs were heard saying that those behind the purification were protesting against the raising of slogans associated with a particular religion, because the ground also happened to be a venue for Ramlilas. 
Chairman C P Radhakrishnan, however, didn't allow anyone besides Kharge and Nadda to speak.
Kharge said he had never told anyone he needed protection because he was a Dalit. "I have the strength to fight, and I do fight. But the purification of the stage made me feel the pain of untouchability and humiliated me," he said.

Radhakrishnan said, "We all condemn untouchability. We are all purified. Those who have done this wrong will be investigated, they should be caught and punished. There are no two opinions on this."
Later, calling the incident "reflective of RSS-BJP's mindset", Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra said PM Narendra Modi must apologise for the caste prejudice shown towards Kharge. AICC general secretary K C Venugopal said the act went "against everything that Ambedkar and the Constitution tell us".

briefs.headline: Opposition claims grand success, says it forced goverment to put off 5 bills
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Terming the monsoon session a grand success, Congress said opposition unity forced Modi govt to defer five legislations that are dangerous for the country, the most important being the one on delimitation for which BJP has been splitting parties to contrive a “tainted majority” in Parliament.
AICC spokesperson Jairam Ramesh and MP Gaurav Gogoi said DMK’s support for the Tamil Nadu assembly resolution against delimitation had smashed the lies spread by BJP that it was close to winning new backing. However, Ramesh said the opposition could not be complacent because BJP had “unlimited resources” at its disposal to try new mischief.
“The TN resolution is a big setback for PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah. No matter how much they try, they will never get the majority for delimitation,” Ramesh said.
Congress said it had also forced the postponement of four key bills — “one nation, one election”, the 130th constitutional amendment bill on automatic dismissal of jailed CMs and ministers, FCRA and Viksit Bharat Shikshan Adhishthan.

Be respectful · TOI community guidelines
Gogoi said the passage of the mines and minerals amendment bill and national cooperative development corporation bill was a matter of concern, but some states would challenge the mines bill in court.
Ramesh said the washout mirrored the one in 2015 over the Vyapam scam, which proved nothing had improved for the youth.
SP MP Dimple Yadav said the insistence on a discussion on “chanda chori” was to show the country how temple donations were being looted under BJP.
DMK spokesman TKS Elangovan said the PM and the home minister evaded Parliament because they were “afraid” of being caught.
Trinamool Congress MP Derek O’Brien said, “This session belonged to the opposition. This was a win for the students and youth.”
Congress has convened a meeting of its apex body, CWC, on Aug 19 to discuss future political strategy.

briefs.headline: Over 11k Indian workers died in Saudi, UAE each in 2021-25, MEA informs Parliament
briefs.bodyText:
Saudi Arabia and the UAE accounted for the vast majority of Indian worker fatalities across Gulf countries from 2021 to 2025 - over 71% of total recorded deaths. According to figures released by ministry of external affairs (MEA) in Parliament on Thursday, Saudi Arabia topped the list with 11,923 deaths, and the UAE was second with 11,489 fatalities. Kuwait reported 3,890 deaths, Oman 2,457, Qatar 1,548 and Bahrain 1,206 deaths. Most nations experienced a sharp spike in deaths in 2021, likely correlated with Covid-19 pandemic, followed by a decline in 2022.
From 2022 onwards, while countries like Bahrain and Qatar registered lower death counts, Saudi Arabia and the UAE recorded upward trends through 2024-2025. Approximately 10 million Indian nationals reside in the six GCC countries, with the UAE alone accounting for 4.5 million Indians.

stories.headline: Darshan has no right to participate in approver proceedings: Karnataka high court
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 In a setback for actor Darshan in the Renukaswamy murder case, the high court Thursday rejected his petition challenging the trial court’s decision not to hear his arguments before deciding on an application by accused no. 14, Pradosh, who has sought to become an approver.
Justice M Nagaprasanna noted that the issue stands completely covered by the decision of the high court in Vinay Kulkarni case which attained finality as a special leave petition against its order was turned down by 
Supreme Court
.
Darshan had challenged the Aug 10 order of the trial court rejecting his plea to provide an audience to address arguments on the application filed by Pradosh. Before the trial court, he had invoked principles of natural justice and the same was rejected.
“The co-accused has no right to say or participate in the pardon proceedings. The right of the co-accused comes into play only when the evidence of the accomplice is recorded before the court as a witness. Till then, co-accused do not have any right,” the trial court had held while relying upon various judgments including the case of Vinay Kulkarni.
The interests of the co-accused are adequately protected at the stage of trial by providing them an opportunity to cross-examine the approver and contest his evidence, the trial court had further pointed out in its order.

stories.headline: Karnataka govt approves rollout of SAMASTA for digitising health records
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Karnataka government has approved the phased rollout of SAMASTA, a digital platform aimed at replacing the mountains of manual records maintained by ASHA workers, Auxiliary Nurse Midwives (ANMs), health inspectors and other community health workers, in a move expected to cut their data-entry workload by around 75%.
The government order issued on Thursday said the platform will digitise registers maintained by field health staff at Ayushman Arogya Kendras, primary health centres and other health facilities. The move follows the announcement in the 2026-27 state Budget to digitise health department field staff records through the SAMASTA mobile application.
SAMASTA will simplify the 485 data elements in the ASHA diary to 134 key data points, reducing duplication and enabling data to be captured at source only once. The platform will work both online and offline and integrate family IDs, Aadhaar-based verification, Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) IDs and other government digital health systems.
The platform will also be integrated with the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), the national digital health ecosystem. The state plans to roll it out in phases after training staff, while ensuring data security, privacy and compliance with ABDM guidelines.
A pilot in Udupi saw 95% beneficiary registration, 85% completion of health check-ups and more than four lakh ABHA IDs linked, according to the government order.
Inset: Rs 10 crore for mental health services in Kalyana Karnataka
The state has also approved Rs 10.04 crore for expanding the Taluk Mental Health Programme across 31 taluks in the Kalyana Karnataka Region, covering Raichur, Yadgir, Bidar, Kalaburagi and Koppal, for 2025-26 and 2026-27. Bidar will have nine taluks under the programme, Kalaburagi seven, while Raichur, Yadgir and Koppal will have five each. The programme aims to strengthen access to mental health services, particularly in rural and underserved areas.

stories.headline: New parking rules seek four-way expansion of paid parking in Bengaluru
stories.bodyText:
Five years after the Karnataka government notified the Directorate of Urban Land Transport’s (DULT) Bengaluru parking policy, the Urban Development Department (UDD) has now come up with a fresh draft of rules, which seeks a major overhaul of the paid parking system in the city.
The fresh draft under the title Greater Bengaluru Authority (Parking) Rules, 2026, has come amidst Bengaluru city corporations exploring fresh sources of revenues. While paid parking was one of the major plans that the new corporations envisioned, all civic bodies, except the central corporation, failed to implement a paid parking system, especially due to lack of demand.
Now, the UDD is planning to implement the system through four different types: developing on-street parking where feasible, developing off-street parking on corporation-owned land, leasing vacant plots for parking, and permitting vacant plot owners or aggregators to provide parking services.
Task force for implementation
The rules propose that each city corporation will have to constitute a parking task force to oversee the preparation and implementation of area parking plans, identify suitable parking areas, and monitor the operation of parking services within its jurisdiction.
The area parking plans and any revisions will be reviewed by the DULT or the Bengaluru Metropolitan Land Transport Authority to ensure compliance with the parking policy and Comprehensive Mobility Plan for Bengaluru. The Chief Commissioner of the GBA will be the competent authority to approve the plans in consultation with the Bengaluru City Police.
Four-way system
For on-street parking, city corporations will be required to develop parking on designated roads in accordance with approved area parking plans.
The draft provides for off-street parking on unused corporation and government land, unallotted civic amenity sites, and, where properties are redeveloped, integration of multi-level parking into corporation properties. Temporary surface parking may also be developed on land under litigation until the legal dispute is resolved.
Vacant private plots could also become a source of parking capacity. City corporations may lease residential, commercial, or industrial vacant plots for parking, with the minimum lease period depending on the infrastructure: three years for surface parking, 10 years for mechanised parking and 15 years for a concrete multi-level car park.
The rules also allow vacant plot owners and third-party aggregators to operate public parking, subject to conditions on access-road width, ownership or lease documents, and exclusive use of the plot for parking.
The draft parking rules propose incentives for vacant plot owners who use their land to provide off-street public parking by exempting them from property tax.
Owners providing multi-level or mechanised parking with a capacity of up to 200 PCUs, but at least 30 PCUs, will be eligible for a 100% exemption from applicable property tax and service charges. For surface-level parking with a capacity of at least 15 PCUs, the plot will be assessed as a vacant site, and 50% of the applicable property tax and service charges will be exempted.
The draft proposes creating more off-street parking facilities around metro stations, major bus stations, and suburban railway stations to encourage commuters to use public transport. The move is also aimed at improving first-mile connectivity.
The transit agencies operating within the GBA limits will have to provide off-street parking on land available with them, particularly in peripheral areas and interchange stations, to facilitate a park-and-ride system. These parking facilities will also be open to members of the public who are not using public transport.
To encourage park-and-ride, transit agencies may offer lower parking rates to public transport users compared to other users. It also proposes the use of integrated technology for parking and transit ticketing.

stories.headline: Bengaluru, parking car outside your house? Pay up to ₹25,000 based on car you own
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru residents who use public roads for parking outside their homes may have to pay an annual fee of up to ₹25,000 or more, depending on the type of car, under the draft Greater Bengaluru Authority (Parking) Rules, 2026, published by the Karnataka Government on Tuesday.
However, it states that residential parking on streets other than arterial and sub-arterial roads may be allowed only for vehicles that have been issued a residential parking permit by the respective city corporation. The permits, however, will be given to only residents of residential buildings that are not in violation of minimum parking requirements specified in the building bylaws.
So, if a resident living in a house with inadequate parking inside the premises, as per building bylaws, parks their car on the roads in front of their houses, it will be deemed illegal and may attract fines under the illegal parking violation by the Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP).
To avoid that, citizens will have to resort to parking at a facility (off-street parking), for which the charges are exorbitant too.
SUV? Pay ₹25,000
The draft rules propose a minimum annual residential parking permit fee of ₹15,000 for hatchbacks, ₹20,000 for sedans, and ₹25,000 for sports utility vehicles (SUVs). The city corporations may also levy an additional administrative fee for issuing the permits, with the amount to be fixed by the GBA Chief Commissioner.
The permit will be issued against a vehicle and the name associated with its registration number. It will be valid for a year and can be renewed annually after verifying that the applicant still lives in the area. The permit will also be valid only on roads designated for residential parking within a walkable distance of the resident’s home. Parking outside the permitted area will also be treated as a violation.
On collector (non-arterial) roads, residential parking will be permitted only if at least six metres of road space remain available for traffic and 1.8 metres of clear walking space are maintained on both sides. On local roads, at least four metres must remain available for traffic, and a 1.8-metre clear footpath must be maintained on at least one side after a vehicle is parked.
Marshals in corporations or other designated employees may verify the validity of permits and report violations to the police. Traffic police will enforce no-parking provisions, including ensuring that only vehicles with valid residential parking permits are allowed in designated residential parking areas. The government has invited objections and suggestions.
The decision has drawn a mixed response. Prajwal Rao, a resident of South Bengaluru, said the rule would place a greater financial burden on people living in rented houses, particularly middle-class families. N.S. Mukunda, founder member of Bengaluru Praja Vedike, said that many citizens would readily pay the amount and obtain permits because it would guarantee them a parking space. However, he said the rule would be difficult to implement in practice and could lead to disputes. “The corporations will have to create off-street parking spaces at a time when there is a severe shortage of vacant land in the city,” he said.

briefs.headline: Rapido to process full medical costs for Bengaluru’s bedridden customer
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 When Sani Krishna,32, became bidridden mid-June following an accident which took place during her bike-taxi ride to work, she had one goal: To fight the aggregator until sufficient compensation is received and to demand accountability.
Thursday, her two-month fight bore partial fruit as Rapido finally agreed to process the entire medical expenses through its insurance partner. A Rapido spokesperson told 
TOI
 that the process will be expedited.
The mobility aggregator revealed that all bike-taxi rides booked through the platform are covered by an insurance policy for both customers and captains. This policy was, however, capped at a maximum of Rs 1 lakh in case of a claim, while her treatment had caused more than Rs 20 lakh.
TOI
 reported on Aug 10 that while Rapido was willing to provide the maximum insurance claim under the policy, it did not accept to pay Sani’s entire medical bills. The accident occurred on June 17 while Sani was commuting between Byrasandra and Domlur for her work. A collision resulted in a tractor running over her.
On Aug 6, Sani’s advocate sent a 
legal notice
 to Rapido demanding an apology and compensation to cover the expenses fully.
Rapido stated that it changed its stance as the accident was an exceptional circumstance. “Given the exceptional circumstances of this case, Rapido has also communicated its willingness to facilitate the processing of the entire eligible medical expense claim, without applying the standard policy cap, subject to the submission and verification of the requisite documentation by the insurer,” the spokesperson clarified.
The aggregator also said it will ensure that Sani’s family receives the full amount towards her medical expenses under the insurance claim.
While Sani had earlier claimed direct compensation from the aggregator instead of depending on a third party, Rapido explained that it is not permitted under applicable law to process insurance claims on behalf of an insurer.
For Sani, who is currently recovering from what she describes as a near-death accident, the update marks a relief. She pointed out that the fight isn’t done: “Rapido still has not communicated to me their decision to insure the entire medical expense. I always had and still have belief that I will overcome this crisis. We also wanted them to take responsibility and apologise for the incident, and it hasn’t happened yet,” she expressed.
Still unable to travel or work, the Bengaluru-based interior designer said she struggles every day. Sani underwent several surgeries, including plastic surgery for her face as she lost multiple teeth and fractured seven ribs.
The circumstances of the accident, including questions relating to the captain’s authorisation and conduct are under investigation, Rapido said.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru woman’s death: 1000 residents protest, officials offer yet another wait
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Anger over the death of 32-year-old Medha Akarsh spilled onto the streets of Ananthnagar Thursday as hundreds of residents gathered to demand a safe and motorable road.
A day after residents staged vocal protests in the south Bengaluru locality, nearly 1,000 people assembled near Venkataramana temple for a meeting with officials of the Hebbagodi city municipal council (CMC). But the meeting ended in frustration, with residents maintaining that officials offered no immediate solutions and instead, walked away amid angry protests.
The residents said the officials informed them that complete restoration of the road could take another three years because of the ongoing Cauvery water supply project.
“It has already been more than five years since we started demanding accountability. Now they are asking us to wait for three more years. People shouted at the officials because there was no concrete solution,” resident Prabhu P said.
The residents insisted they are not asking for anything extraordinary other than a road that can be safely used. “We cannot continue waiting for three more years. All we demand is basic infrastructure. 
Even if they level the road now, it turns into slush every time it rains. We also wanted the MLA to meet us, but he did not turn up,” said Abhishek G, another resident.
The protesters pointed out that the roads remain choked with dust during summer and slush during monsoon, making commuting hazardous. Besides poor roads, they highlighted the absence of footpaths and streetlights across the locality.
In a memorandum submitted to CMC, the residents said the deteriorating roads have led to frequent accidents, health problems and daily hardship for thousands of commuters. They noted that the stretch is used every day by children attending 13 schools and 15 preschools, besides employees travelling towards Sarjapur, Marathahalli and Whitefield.
“The Fruit Market Road, in particular, is in a highly dangerous condition and urgently requires attention. We request the authorities to immediately lay new roads and ensure the safety of residents, schoolchildren and commuters,” Abhishek said.
Local civic activist Sophia Sebastian said accidents have become routine in the area. “Heavy vehicles and tankers ply on these roads throughout the day. Just two or three months ago, several people were injured and children suffered fractures. Even after someone has lost her life, there is still no end to the civic mess,” she said.
Rajendra BL, commissioner of Hebbagodi CMC, said the Cauvery water supply project is a three-year exercise and permanent asphalting cannot be taken up immediately.
“Within a week, all underground drainage work will be completed. The engineers have committed to it. We need another three to four months to restore the road properly; otherwise, it will sink again,” he told 
TOI
.
He added that officials have been directed to clear completed work zones and fill potholes within a week.
Meanwhile, several residents who participated in Wednesday night’s and Thursday morning’s protests were reportedly detained by police for allegedly holding demonstrations without permission. The protesters maintained they had no option but to take to the streets after Medha’s death, saying the tragedy should finally compel the authorities to deliver the basic infrastructure they have been demanding for years.

briefs.headline: Freedom Habba in Bengaluru on August 15: What visitors need to know
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Around 18,000 people have registered for Saturday’s Freedom Habba, Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) said Thursday. To ensure safety and crowd management, only those with pre-booked registrations and QR-code access will be allowed entry.
GBA officials confirmed no on-the-spot or late registrations will be permitted; every participant must pre-register to gain access to the habba. Entry will be free only for those below 12 years of age.
The habba, scheduled from 12pm to 10pm, has been divided into three segments. The first, from 12pm to 3pm, will feature stalls and other activities. The second, from 3pm to 5pm, will be dedicated to the parade, while the final segment, from 5pm to 10pm, will include live concerts, stage programmes and a fireworks display.
Officials said participants registered for a particular segment will be allowed entry only during that segment to ensure smooth crowd management and enable wider public participation.
Facilities at venue
* 80 bio-toilets set up, including 30 in Vidhana Soudha and 50 outside the premises
* Drinking water distribution counters set up at key locations
* “May I Help You?” volunteers, identifiable through designated T-shirts, deployed to assist visitors
* Additional Metro and bus services to operate after programme to help participants reach home
* Two fire tenders stationed at venue
* Two first-aid centres equipped with beds and medical personnel
* Four ambulances staffed with paramedical personnel stationed in different directions and will be linked to designated hospitals for emergency response
* Women’s help centre set up, which will include breastfeeding room, resting facilities and sanitary amenities
Vidhana Soudha Metro station to be closed
Dr BR Ambedkar Metro station, Vidhana Soudha, will be closed Saturday from 10am to 9.30pm for the habba. 
Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) said the decision was taken on the advice of Bengaluru Central City Corporation commissioner, as part of public safety and crowd management measures. During the closure, passengers can use Cubbon Park station or Sir M Visvesvaraya station, Central College.
Trains will pass through Vidhana Soudha station without stopping. From 9.30pm, entry into the station will be permitted, BMRCL said.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru health inspector takes bribe from salon owner, suspended
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Bengaluru North City Corporation (BNCC) suspended a senior health inspector for allegedly accepting a bribe from a salon owner in Yelahanka in connection with trade licence-related work. Rais Ahmed Aziz Mianavar from Yelahanka division was suspended with immediate effect under Rule 10(1)(a) of Karnataka Civil Services (CCA) Rules, 1957.
According to the order, the corporation received a complaint alleging that Rais Ahmed had demanded and accepted money from a hair salon owner in connection with the business’s trade licence and a health department inspection. Sources said Rais Ahmed fainted while he was caught taking bribe.
The official, however, denied taking any illegal money from the salon owner.
A video purportedly showing the alleged bribe-taking surfaced on social media on Aug 12. Following this, the BNCC health officer (public health) submitted a report recommending disciplinary action against the official.
The suspension order said the alleged conduct amounted to serious dereliction of duty and violated Karnataka Government Servants’ Conduct Rules. A departmental inquiry has been kept pending against the official.
During the suspension, Rais Ahmed will be entitled to a subsistence allowance under the Karnataka Civil Services Rules and cannot leave the headquarters without prior permission.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru ORR white-topping work from October 2026
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Greater Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda has directed officials to begin white-topping works on Outer Ring Road (ORR) in Oct and complete them by Jan 2027, while also rolling out a series of pedestrian and traffic-management measures along the corridor for the Rs 450-crore ORR redevelopment project.
At a review meeting Thursday, the minister instructed agencies to build continuous three-metre-wide footpaths, remove encroachments, identify private transformers installed in public spaces, and create designated bus/taxi pick-up and drop-off points wherever space is available. Officials were asked to construct bus bays on the main carriageway.
To reduce traffic disruption during the work, Byre Gowda said officials have been directed to engage with companies along ORR and facilitate 50% work-from-home arrangements. The minister asked agencies to use internal roads for traffic diversions and consult Outer Ring Road Companies’ Association (ORRCA) and traffic police before finalising mobility plans.
At a recent ORRCA meeting attended by over 100 company representatives, nearly 70% urged govt to focus on completing the Metro network before launching new ORR projects. Citing delays and poor infrastructure, companies said confidence in authorities’ execution capabilities has weakened, a concern shared by their global headquarters.

briefs.headline: On-street parking may get costlier in Bengaluru as new draft rules aim to promote off-street parking
briefs.deck: ‘On-street parking’ refers to parking on roads, while ‘off-street parking’ refers to parking in non-road locations, including vacant plots
briefs.bodyText:
Parking in Bengaluru could become more expensive, with the draft Greater Bengaluru Authority (Parking) Rules, 2026, proposing minimum charges based on the category of the road and whether the parking is on-street or off-street, representing a steep increase from the current rates.
“On-street parking” refers to parking on roads, while “off-street parking” refers to parking in non-road locations, including vacant plots.
For on-street parking, the minimum hourly fee has been proposed at ₹20 to ₹40 for two-wheelers and ₹40 to ₹80 for light motor vehicles (LMVs). For off-street parking, the minimum hourly fee has been proposed at ₹10 to ₹20 for two-wheelers and ₹20 to ₹40 for LMVs.
The draft also proposes monthly off-street parking rates. Those opting for off-street parking only at night, between 8 p.m. and 8 a.m., may be charged 50% of the monthly off-street parking fee.
Road categories
Before implementing the rules, city corporations will categorise roads into three types: Categories A, B and C. The parking charges will vary depending on the category of the road where the vehicle is parked.
A commercial road that predominantly attracts people from across the city may be categorised as Category A. Commercial roads that attract people from surrounding neighbourhoods may be categorised as Category B, while other commercial roads catering largely to local residents may be categorised as Category C.
Currently, across the city, two-wheelers have to pay ₹15 per hour, and four-wheelers have to pay ₹25 per hour. The rationale behind the steep hike is to encourage off-street parking. However, in major commercial hubs, this is likely to affect officegoers.
In addition, stretches with a paid parking system already may move to a new charge structure, according to the draft.
Parking longer costs more
The proposed system also seeks to discourage long-duration on-street parking. Parking for more than two hours would attract exponentially higher charges, particularly where off-street parking is available nearby. City corporations may also introduce different rates for peak and non-peak hours, though the minimum and maximum rates at a parking facility cannot differ by more than 50%.
The draft further states that parking charges would be periodically increased based on demand and supply, with revised rates to be notified by the GBA chief commissioner. stories.headline: ​A predictable rise: On inflation
stories.deck: Inflation will remain high in the foreseeable future
stories.bodyText:
A rise in India’s July retail inflation was a foregone conclusion, but its modest increase, at 4.45%, up from 4.38% in June, is still the highest in 19 months, since December 2024. This is the second consecutive month that retail inflation has stayed above the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)’s 4% target, even while remaining comfortably within its 2%-6% tolerance range. Predictably, it has again been driven by food, fuel and transport, even as core inflation, excluding precious metals, has remained below 3%. What is telling is the extent of rural, food-led inflation, which rose from 5.45% in June to 5.79% in July, while urban food inflation decreased marginally from 5.09% to 5.05%. Staples such as onion (22.54%), garlic (35.36%) and ginger (83.62%) fuelled the rise, even as potato (-16.56%) and tomato (-4.59%) moderated. Transport, however, continues to have a wider impact, pointing to elevated input-cost pressures. Transport inflation quickened to 4.43% in July from 4.31% in June, while the crucial subdivision, transport services for goods, rose from 7.70% to 7.77%. Despite the July 1 cut in commercial LPG prices of about ₹183, food and beverage serving services inflation quickened to 7.75% in July, indicating that restaurants are yet to recoup revenues and margins lost following the steep operating costs from March through May. Commercial LPG was cut by a further ₹202 on August 1, but this is unlikely to immediately bring down menu prices.
The monsoon remains a concern, with parts of western, central and southern India remaining rain-deficient. Precious metals inflation, particularly gold (32.98%) and silver (109.84%), moderated, but remains extraordinarily high. Crude prices were relatively stable during the July CPI reference period, but began rising again in August. More worryingly, Ukraine-related disruptions around Russia’s Black Sea export infrastructure, particularly Novorossiysk, could raise freight and risk premiums for Russian crude. Russia supplied nearly half of India’s crude imports in June, making such disruptions relevant to India’s landed energy costs. The rupee also depreciated by about 1.6% between the June 15 and July 15 CPI reference dates, further amplifying imported inflation. In the background, there are signs of weakening economic momentum, with the HSBC composite PMI showing a sharp fall from 57.1 in June to 54.3 in July, its weakest expansion since March 2022. While the PMI is a high-frequency indicator and need not reflect a long-term trend, it is nevertheless worth taking note of. The RBI’s Monetary Policy Committee, which held the repo rate at 5.25% for the fourth consecutive meeting in August, is therefore likely to remain on hold through the second quarter of FY27, as it weighs persistent supply-side inflation against weakening economic momentum.

stories.headline: Mining Amendment law does not impinge upon States’ rights: Minister
stories.deck: Coal and Mines Minister G. Kishan Reddy says the legislation extends to only major minerals across eleven States
stories.bodyText:
The Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, passed in Parliament on Thursday (August 13, 2026), does not seek to impinge upon the rights of States over their resources, Union Minister for Coal and Mines G. Kishan Reddy said on the day. The legislation is primarily aimed at ensuring growth and equitability in the overall ecosystem, he told reporters here.
The Minister said the amendment encompasses only certain major minerals and does not extend to minor minerals over which the States retain absolute control.
“The government’s primary objective is to ensure identical [taxation] rates across the board to ensure [effective prices] do not spike. We are neither seeking to impinge upon any State’s rights nor acquire any control [over States’ resources],” he stated.
Seeking to clarify the standing on minor minerals, Mr. Reddy said, “It [the ratified legislation] does not change the revenue dynamics for minor minerals, neither for its exploration, production, land acquisition, instituting blocks, auctioneering as well as its levying of State taxes and cess.”
According to a memo circulated by the government, the list of major minerals includes coal, lignite, iron ore, graphite, cobalt, lithium and nickel among others.
Further, the provision of the law encompasses only 11 States: Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Goa.
Arguing that the Union government has ensured flow of revenue to States, he reported that States’ share in overall mineral revenues have accelerated from 65% to 88% between fiscal year 2014-15 and 2024-25. That from has elevated to 96% from 55% during the same period.
Separately, Mr. Reddy also told reporters that the proposed legislation would be seeking to put forth a suitable structure for the proposed coal and minerals exchange.
“We want to enable reforms that would help spur the production of major minerals,” he stated, adding, “In [the proposed] exchange, differing rates would hamper the market for entities with higher prices. Thus, similar prices become important.”
Separately, officials also informed that India is expected to have its first coal exchange in the “eight to nine months”.
The Rajya Sabha on Wednesday (August 12) passed the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, which, among other things, seeks that States do not levy any tax or cess on mineral bearing lands and their operations. The now-ratified legislation had drawn opposition from States, especially Kerala, for “overriding” federal structure and encroaching upon their constitutional powers.

stories.headline: India’s critical mineral push: Govt plans processing parks in 4 states
stories.deck: India is set to establish four specialized parks dedicated to critical mineral processing, targeting lithium and nickel first. The initiative, spearheaded by state governments with central technical assistance, is aligned with the National Critical Mineral Mission aimed at bolstering self-reliance. This move is crucial in propelling India’s transition toward green energy, ensuring a sustainable…
stories.bodyText:
India's critical mineral roadmap is advancing, with the government set to establish four dedicated critical mineral processing parks in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha. The initial focus will be on building domestic processing capacity for lithium and nickel, mines secretary Keshav Chandra said on Thursday.
The proposed parks will be developed around specific minerals, creating dedicated ecosystems that bring processing and downstream industries together. Lithium and nickel have been prioritised because of their importance to the battery sector, while processing for other critical minerals will be taken up subsequently.
“We are fast-tracking lithium and nickel because these are crucial elements for the battery sector. Batteries are currently the most important component globally for future growth; so, we will fast-track both of these,” Chandra said while briefing reporters.
The government will soon introduce measures for the two minerals and is in the process of identifying designated parks, he said.
“Batteries are currently the most important component globally for future growth. 
So, we are fast-tracking both of these.....we will introduce measures for these two very soon, and we are identifying designated parks for them,” Chandra added.
Each park will be designed to house the complete value chain for a designated element, from processing to downstream industries. This will allow value addition across different stages to be carried out within a single location, the official said.
State governments will take the lead in planning and implementing the parks, while the Centre will provide technical support. Coal and Mines Minister G Kishan Reddy said the Centre had already written to all state governments and chief ministers seeking their cooperation.
“The planning itself will be by the state government. We will extend full technical support,” he said.
The proposed parks form part of the National Critical Mineral Mission (NCMM), which the government had earlier approved with a total outlay of Rs 34,300 crore over seven years. The mission aims to achieve self-reliance in critical minerals and accelerate India's journey towards green energy transition.
The government has earmarked Rs 16,300 crore for the mission, while public sector enterprises are expected to contribute Rs 18,000 crore. The NCMM also seeks to promote exploration of critical minerals within the country and offshore locations.
Critical minerals such as copper, lithium, nickel, cobalt and rare earths are essential raw materials for clean energy technologies. Their applications span wind turbines, electricity networks, electric vehicles and battery manufacturing.

stories.headline: US wholesale inflation slows to 4.7% in July: What comes next for Fed, consumers
stories.deck: In July, wholesale prices in the United States exhibited a cooling trend, providing a much-needed breath of fresh air. The decline in energy costs significantly reduced producer price pressures throughout the month. While consumer inflation also saw a slight dip, financial constraints persist for many households. Notably, wholesale inflation excluding food and energy showed improvement…
stories.bodyText:
Wholesale prices in the US cooled in July, offering a welcome sign that inflation may be losing some momentum as lower energy costs helped ease price pressures.
Data released by the labor department showed that the producer price index (PPI), which tracks prices received by producers before they reach consumers, increased 4.7% from a year earlier in July. That marked a decline from the 5.5% annual rise recorded in June. Compared with the previous month, wholesale prices were flat, following a 0.1% fall in June.
The moderation in producer prices came a day after government figures showed a modest cooling in consumer inflation as well. Despite that, household budgets remain under pressure, with consumer prices continuing to rise faster than wages for the fourth straight month. Higher costs for essentials, including rent and utilities, could weigh on spending if incomes fail to keep pace.
Underlying price pressures also softened during the month. Excluding food and energy, core wholesale inflation eased to 4.2% year-on-year in July from 4.7% in June. On a monthly basis, core prices rose 0.2%, slower than the 0.4% increase recorded between May and June.
The decline in inflation was aided by lower fuel costs earlier in July, when gas prices retreated after surging during the Iran war. 
However, fuel prices moved higher again later in the month and into early August, creating uncertainty over whether inflation could accelerate in the next set of data.
“The soft (producer prices) reading for July points to reduced inflationary pressure for businesses in coming months,” said Ben Ayers, senior economist at Nationwide. “While the renewed rise in fuel costs is concerning, input costs beyond energy are cooling.”
The latest figures are likely to feature in discussions at the Federal Reserve ahead of its September policy meeting. Officials have so far left interest rates unchanged this year and are weighing whether inflation is easing enough to avoid further rate increases.
Economists closely track producer prices because some components, particularly healthcare and financial services, feed into the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) index, the inflation measure preferred by the Fed. The PCE report is due in about two weeks.
Based on the consumer and producer inflation reports released so far, economists expect core PCE inflation to remain at around 3.3% in July when the data is published on August 26. That would suggest inflation remains above the Fed’s 2% target even as other measures show some easing.
At the same time, signs of a softer labour market are adding another factor to the Fed’s deliberations. Government data released last week showed employers cut jobs in July, pointing to economic weakness that could reduce the case for higher borrowing costs.

briefs.headline: Anchor investors sell 50% of IPO holdings after a year:SEBI
briefs.deck: Mutual Funds were notably more conservative than FPIs.
briefs.bodyText:
Anchor investors offload 50% of their initial public offering (IPO) holdings 30 days after the completion of 12 months from the date of listing, according to a Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) report.
Market regulator SEBI analysed data of 242 mainboard IPOs listed during April 2022 to October 2025, in its paper titled “Study on Exit Behaviour of Anchor Investors in Mainboard IPOs,” authored by Laltu Pore and Pampana Hari Nayak Akshay, officers in the Department of Economic and Policy Analysis (DEPA).
The exit at initial stages after the listing date is just about 3.2%, but this gradually increases as the lock-in period expires, going up till 50%, 30 days after the one year has passed since the listing day.
“First exit was approximately 3% for both categories, rising to (about) 8% at 60 days. At the 90-day mark, issues made under Regulation 6(1) recorded an exit of approximately 18.5% while those made under Regulation 6(2) showed approximately 15.3%, suggesting marginally lower cumulative exit in the latter,” the authors said.
Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) constituted the largest share of nearly 44% in anchor allotment, followed by mutual funds with 39%. The former however contributes the most of the exits.
“Mutual Funds were notably more conservative than FPIs. Post the first lock-in expiry,104 IPOs showed zero MF exit (among the highest zero-exit counts) and 83 IPOs were in the range of >0–25% bucket. Even by the 90-day stage, MF exit remained more restrained: 41 zero-exit IPOs, 111 in >0–25%, 31 in >25–50%, and only 6 in >50–99%, with no 100% exit instances. This indicates MFs are more patient holders of their anchor allocations,” the authors observed.
The report assumes significance in light of the Chief Economic Adviser’s observation that IPOs were increasingly becoming exit routes. While his comments were directed at early-stage investors, a similar trend can be seen among anchor investors, many of whom show strong enthusiasm for IPOs but gradually exited once the lock-in period ends. Consequently, several much-hyped IPO stocks trade below their offer prices within a year of listing, while some never recover to their initial offering levels.
FPIs dominated in absolute exit value across all three stages, contributing about ₹1,750crore at first exit (about 3% of anchor allotment to FPIs), ₹4,800 crore (about 9%) at 60-day mark, and ₹10,400 crore(about 20%) at second exit. “This confirms FPIs not only exit a higher percentage of their anchor holdings, but also generate the largest quantum of secondary market supply by a wide margin, given their larger allotment base,” the report said.
MFs were the second largest source by value: about ₹1,300 crore at first exit (about 3% of anchor allotment to MFs), ₹3,200 crore (about 7%) at exit-60 day, and ₹6,800 crore (about 15%) at second exit. While MF exit intensity (%) is lower than FPIs, their large allotment base “still translates into significant absolute supply”, it said.

briefs.headline: India’s Q1 pharma exports up 6.8% to $8.1bn; U.S. remains largest export destination
briefs.deck: NAFTA (North American Free Trade Agreement), Europe, Africa and Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) continued to be the key destinations region-wise, accounting for nearly 75% of the export
briefs.bodyText:
India’s pharmaceutical exports rose 6.8% year-on-year (YoY) to $8.1 billion in the first quarter (Q1) ended June, according to the Pharmaceuticals Export Promotion Council of India (Pharmexcil).
Drug formulations and biologicals exports stood at $5.98 billion, registering a 4.14% YoY increase and accounting for 73.85% of total exports. Bulk drugs and drug intermediates, the second-largest export category, grew by 13.84% YoY to $1.36 billion, vaccine exports by 35.68% YoY to $0.39 billion. and surgical products exports by 11.95% YoY to $0.21 billion.
The broad-based growth reflects sustained global demand for affordable generic medicines, increasing procurement from regulated and emerging markets and India’s growing strength as a pharmaceutical manufacturing and export hub, said the pharma exporters body, under the Ministry of Commerce.
NAFTA (North American Free Trade Agreement), Europe, Africa and Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) together continued to be the key destinations region-wise, accounting for nearly 75% of the exports. NAFTA alone was the largest market, accounting for 34.28% of the exports.
Country-wise, the U.S. remained India’s largest pharmaceutical export destination, followed by Brazil, the U.K, the Netherlands, and France. The top 25 export destinations, during the quarter, accounted for nearly 70% of pharmaceutical exports, with shipments valued at $5.65 billion, which was 5.50% YoY growth.
“The export performance demonstrates the sector continues to combine scale in established markets with growing momentum across a wider set of geographies. The U.S. remains our largest export destination, with shipments valued at $2.50 billion and a 30.89% share, while the strong performance of Brazil, the Netherlands, France and several emerging markets reflects the expanding global footprint of Indian pharmaceutical companies,” Pharmexcil Chairman Namit Joshi said.
The double-digit growth recorded across Europe, Africa, Latin America, ASEAN and South Asia is important in the present global trade environment. The ability to combine quality, regulatory credibility, manufacturing scale and market diversification will determine strength of India’s next phase of pharmaceutical export growth, he said.
In June, pharmaceutical shipments increased 7.13% to $2.81 billion ($2.62 billion). June exports were 6.86% higher compared to $2.63 billion in May FY27, Pharmexcil said.
India’s pharmaceutical exports in FY26 increased more than 2% YoY to $31.11 billion.

briefs.headline: US stock market today: Wall Street moves towards all-time high as inflation moderates and oil prices drop
briefs.deck: Investor sentiment improved after government data showed wholesale prices in the United States were 4.7% higher in the latest month compared with a year earlier.
briefs.bodyText:
US stock market today: Wall Street benchmarks moved closer to record territory on Thursday after fresh data suggested inflationary pressures continued to ease. Markets also found support from another decline in oil prices, extending their recent volatile swings.
The S&P 500 advanced 0.8%, putting it on course to surpass the record high it reached last week. As of 10:15 a.m. Eastern time, the Dow Jones Industrial Average had gained 185 points, or 0.3%, while the Nasdaq Composite was up 1%.
Inflation moderates
Investor sentiment improved after government data showed wholesale prices in the United States were 4.7% higher in the latest month compared with a year earlier, according to an AP report. Although the pace of inflation remained elevated, it was lower than June's 5.5% reading and also came in slightly below economists' expectations.
A continued moderation in inflation could give the Federal Reserve greater room to delay raising interest rates. While higher borrowing costs help curb inflation, they also slow economic activity by increasing the cost of credit for households and businesses.
The latest wholesale inflation figures, coming a day after softer consumer inflation data, have reduced expectations of an imminent rate hike. According to CME Group data, traders now see only a 35% probability that the Fed will raise its benchmark interest rate at its September meeting, down from roughly 50% just two days earlier.
If the central bank does decide to raise rates, it would mark the first increase in more than three years. Such a move could also draw criticism from President Donald Trump, who has been urging the Fed to lower interest rates.
The bond market reflected the changing expectations, with Treasury yields moving lower, providing additional support to equities. The yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury note declined to 4.61% from 4.68% at Wednesday's close and 4.72% on Monday. Even so, it remained well above the 3.97% level seen before the conflict with Iran drove oil and gasoline prices sharply higher.
Oil prices drop
Oil prices also retreated on Thursday, helping ease concerns over inflation. Brent crude fell 3.3% to $86.02 a barrel.
Oil prices have remained highly volatile in recent weeks. During the previous month alone, Brent crude fluctuated between $72 and $102 a barrel as optimism and pessimism over a possible resolution to the conflict repeatedly shifted expectations about when oil tankers could resume unrestricted movement through the Middle East and restore global crude supplies.
Stock-wise
On Wall Street, real estate stocks were among the strongest performers. Falling interest rates and lower bond yields tend to make the dividend payouts offered by many real estate investment trusts (REITs) more appealing to investors. Lower mortgage rates could also encourage greater activity in the housing sector.
Apartment owner AvalonBay Communities gained 2.6%, while Builders FirstSource, a supplier of countertops and other construction materials, advanced 3.4%.
The decline in oil prices also supported companies with significant fuel expenses by improving expectations that their operating costs could ease. United Airlines rose 1.7%, while cruise operator Carnival added 2.9%.
Restaurant chain Jack in the Box climbed 7.3% after reporting quarterly earnings that exceeded analysts' expectations. Strong corporate earnings have been a key driver behind Wall Street's rally, as stock prices generally move in line with companies' long-term profit growth.
These gains helped offset weakness in Cisco Systems, whose shares fell 7% despite reporting quarterly revenue and profit that surpassed Wall Street forecasts. Analysts said investors appeared concerned about the company's future profit margins. Cisco's stock has also remained under pressure through the summer amid broader concerns that valuations across AI-related stocks had risen too rapidly.
Overseas, equity markets delivered a mixed performance across Europe and Asia. South Korea's Kospi was again among the world's strongest-performing indices, rising 3.6%. Seoul has witnessed some of the sharpest swings in AI-linked stocks because its market is heavily influenced by technology giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.

briefs.headline: What Trump tariffs? Russia now supplies more than half of India’s crude oil imports
briefs.deck: According to GTRI’s analysis, in June India imported crude oil worth $14.8 billion from all sources, of which $7.2 billion came from Russia. This translated into a Russian share of 48.6%.
briefs.bodyText:
With Russia’s share in India’s oil imports progressively climbing up, any abrupt shift away from Moscow’s crude appears unlikely in wake of the fresh Trump tariff threat emerging from the US, says Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) in its latest report.
According to GTRI’s analysis, Russia accounted for over 50% of India’s crude oil imports in July.
“Russia supplied an estimated 52% of India’s crude-oil imports in July 2026, up from 48.6% in June. The estimate indicates that more than half of India’s imported crude now comes from Russia, sharply limiting New Delhi’s ability to reduce these purchases at short notice,” says GTRI founder Ajay Srivastava.
Also Read | 
100% tariffs: Why India may ignore Trump threat and continue buying Russian crude oil
Russia a major supplier for India
According to GTRI’s analysis, in June India imported crude oil worth $14.8 billion from all sources, of which $7.2 billion came from Russia. This translated into a Russian share of 48.6%.
For July, the government released data showing India's overall imports from Russia at $8.9 billion but did not disclose how much of that consisted of crude oil. Since crude accounted for 82% of India's imports from Russia in June, GTRI applied the same proportion to July's figures, estimating Russian crude imports at around $7.3 billion.
India's crude sourcing pattern has undergone a major transformation.
India's dependence on Russian crude has risen sharply over the past few years. Russia's share in India's crude oil imports climbed from around 15% in 2022 to 30.3% in FY2025-26. This has only gone up in recent months amid the US-Iran war.
At the same time, the combined contribution of Gulf suppliers has declined significantly, dropping from more than 55% in 2022 to below 30% by June 2026. The conflict involving Iran and the resulting disruptions to global supply chains further accelerated this shift, increasing the importance of Russian crude in meeting India's energy needs.
What the US bill for sanctions on Russia could mean
The proposed US sanctions could leave India facing a difficult decision.
If the proposed US legislation on Russian sanctions is enacted, India could be exposed to additional tariffs of up to 100% should it continue importing Russian energy.
“The measure could force India to choose between reducing its Russian oil purchases and protecting its exports to the US,” says Srivastava.
However, he notes that India has limited room to make an abrupt shift.
What the Russia sanctions bill means
“Replacing a supplier that now accounts for more than half of imported crude would be difficult, costly and potentially disruptive. Alternative suppliers may not be able to provide comparable volumes immediately or on equally favourable commercial terms,” he says.
A sharp cut in Russian crude imports could raise India's oil import bill, disrupt refinery operations, widen the trade deficit and add to inflationary pressures. It could also increase the country's dependence on an already volatile West Asian region, Srivastava adds.
According to the GTRI founder, India should continue buying Russian crude oil.
“Discounted Russian crude has lowered India’s import costs, diversified its supplies and strengthened energy security. India should continue purchasing Russian oil as long as it remains commercially attractive and complies with applicable rules,” he says.
“American tariff threats should not determine India’s energy policy. Differences with Washington should be addressed through firm negotiations, not unilateral concessions that raise India’s energy costs and weaken its strategic autonomy,” he adds.

briefs.headline: India has “reassuring” talks with U.S., including on Bill that proposes 100% tariffs

briefs.bodyText:
India has had “reassuring” recent discussions with the U.S. including on a proposed law that would see tariffs of 100% being imposed on India and other countries that import Russian oil in large quantities, a senior official in the government said on the condition of anonymity.

Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which proposes tariffs of up to 100% on countries that import oil from Russia in large quantities. Under the criteria laid out in the Bill, these tariffs would apply on India and four other countries, if it becomes law.
The Bill awaits introduction and voting in the House of Representatives before it can become law.
“We are engaged with the U.S. on the trade deal, and have had discussions on the Russia sanctions bill,” the official said. “The conversations have been reassuring.”
India currently faces a 10% tariff on 55% of what it exports to the U.S., a result of a U.S. investigation into whether India and other countries had done enough to stop the import of goods made using forced labour.
A second investigation, on whether these countries are using excess capacity to export to the U.S., could see further tariffs being levied on India. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal, however, said that India is engaged with the U.S. on these matters.
“We are engaged with the U.S. side on the trade deal,” Mr. Agrawal said at a press conference on Thursday in response to a query from The Hindu. “Both sides are committed to the deal that we have agreed to on February 3, 2026, and for which the joint statement was issued on February 7, 2026.”
While the joint statement mentions tariff levels that have now become moot due to the Supreme Court’s cancellation of the U.S. reciprocal tariffs, it also includes a line that says the U.S. and India “commit to provide each other preferential market access in sectors of respective interest on a sustained basis”.

stories.headline: Ronaldo and Georgina’s secret wedding had just 5 people present with Zero outside guests
stories.deck: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez kept their August 11 wedding in Cascais remarkably private, reportedly limiting the ceremony to themselves and their five children. The couple had faced intense speculation over the guest list, location and arrangements before secretly marrying and confirming the news afterwards. Their intimate ceremony contrasted sharply with false reports that had drawn…
stories.bodyText:
Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez chose to keep their wedding almost entirely away from the public eye, and the first details emerging from the ceremony suggest they succeeded. After nearly a decade together, the couple reportedly married in a private civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, with the occasion centred not on footballers, celebrities or a large circle of friends, but on their family.
The scale of the ceremony is particularly striking given the extraordinary attention surrounding their relationship in the days before they finally confirmed they were married.
Ronaldo and Georgina kept the ceremony intimate
Ronaldo and Rodriguez married in Cascais on August 11, bringing an end to years of speculation over when they would formalise their relationship.
The couple announced the marriage themselves with a photograph of their wedding bands on Instagram, accompanied by the simple caption “C❤️G.” A representative for Ronaldo subsequently confirmed that the ceremony was held in Cascais and described it as an “intimate and private” occasion.
The secrecy surrounding the wedding had fuelled considerable speculation in the buildup, with reports and rumours ranging from the guest list and wedding arrangements to how much the couple might spend on the ceremony. 
However, there has still been no definitive public account of the wedding’s guest list or overall arrangements.
The closest indication came from Ronaldo’s representative, who told the 
Daily Mail
 that the ceremony was “a private and intimate moment attended by their five children.” The representative said: “Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez were married today in a civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, and are now officially husband and wife.”
If that account is accurate, and the five children were the only people present apart from Ronaldo and Rodriguez, it would mean the ceremony had no outside guests, making the already private wedding even smaller than many of the rumours surrounding it had suggested.
The five children were the centre of the guest list
Ronaldo and Rodriguez have five children between them, with two being Rodriguez's biological children and the other three being Ronaldo's children from before his relationship with Rodriguez began.
Their presence meant the ceremony remained firmly centred on the family the couple have built together rather than becoming a high-profile celebrity event.
That privacy appears to have been deliberate. There had been no confirmed details about the ceremony beforehand, leaving supporters and the media to speculate about everything from the location to the scale of the wedding.
Instead, Ronaldo and Rodriguez reportedly chose a civil ceremony in Cascais and revealed the marriage only afterwards.
The contrast with the speculation surrounding their wedding could hardly have been greater.
Hundreds of fans had already gone looking for the wrong wedding
Only days before Ronaldo and Rodriguez confirmed their marriage, attention had been focused on Funchal Cathedral in Madeira.
Reports had claimed the couple would marry there on August 8, prompting hundreds of fans, journalists and well-wishers to gather outside the cathedral in Ronaldo's hometown.
The reports proved false.
The wedding taking place at the cathedral belonged to another Portuguese couple, Fabio Ramos and Fatima Nicole Cunha Teixeira, rather than Ronaldo and Rodriguez. The extraordinary confusion left the genuine wedding location completely out of the spotlight.
That episode also gave Ronaldo the opportunity to see the lighter side of the speculation. When footage and photographs circulated showing crowds waiting outside the church for him and Rodriguez, he reacted with laughing emojis on social media.
The real wedding was subsequently revealed to have taken place in Cascais, rather than Madeira, and to have been considerably more private than the crowds gathered in Funchal had anticipated.
A decade-long relationship ends with a quiet ceremony
Ronaldo and Rodriguez began their relationship in 2016, when Rodriguez was working at a Gucci store in Madrid.
Rodriguez later recalled in her Netflix series 
I Am Georgina
 that Ronaldo would sometimes collect her from work, including once in a Bugatti, despite her arriving at the store by bus.
She left the job later that year after fans began gathering outside the shop, and the couple made their first public appearance together at The Best FIFA Football Awards in January 2017.
They subsequently built a family together, with Ronaldo's twins Mateo and Eva born via surrogacy in June 2017 and Rodriguez giving birth to their daughter Alana Martina later that year.
Ronaldo had previously made clear that he intended to marry Rodriguez after the 2026 World Cup, but the couple gave the public no reliable indication of the ceremony's actual timing or location.
That secrecy continued right up to the end.
After the wedding,
Ronaldo and Rodriguez were seen together
 at Lisbon's Humberto Delgado Airport, accompanied by their children. According to Portuguese media, they entered through a VIP access point, with Saudi Arabia believed to be their likely destination.

stories.headline: ​Sticks and goals: On India at the FIH Hockey World Cup 2026
stories.deck: India might see its best finish in 50 years in hockey World Cup
stories.bodyText:
When India celebrates its 80th Independence Day, its men’s hockey team will open its World Cup campaign against Wales in Amstelveen, aiming to end a 51-year medal drought. Because of hockey’s emotional connection with Indians, the wait has been agonising for the eight-time Olympic champion. It won its last medal when the Ajit Pal Singh-led side lifted the trophy in Kuala Lumpur in 1975 during the pre-synthetic turf era. Trust in the present Harmanpreet Singh-captained side has grown after India broke a 41-year Olympic jinx with bronze in Tokyo in 2021 and retained it in Paris 2024. Under coach Craig Fulton, the team won Asian Games gold in 2023, Olympic bronze in 2024, and the Asia Cup in 2025, with the last one helping it qualify for the World Cup. Despite finishing eighth in the FIH Pro League 2025-26, India showed positive signs by beating World champion Germany and Olympic champion the Netherlands. After experiencing experimentation, defeats and two controversies — involving most-capped player Manpreet Singh, and the unwarranted decision to change the jersey from the familiar blue to saffron, the squad has regrouped for its first World Cup following the retirement of legendary custodian P.R. Sreejesh. After Wales, the eighth-ranked side faces a formidable England and traditional rival Pakistan in the pool.
Comprising two-time Olympic medallists and promising youngsters, the team, placed sixth and ninth in the last two editions, now targets a higher finish in the World Cup before embarking next month on a mission to retain the Asian Games gold, which will earn it a berth in the 2028 Olympics. The Salima Tete-led women’s team has rebuilt under Dutchman Sjoerd Marijne after turmoil caused first by the exit of his predecessor and then by an alleged sexual harassment case involving a former Hockey India official. Marijne, who took India to its best-ever fourth in Tokyo in his first stint, guided it to World Cup qualification and Nations Cup victory. Despite the Hockey India League experience and the exposure to foreign players, the team of five 200-cap players and 11 debutants may find it tough to match 1974’s fourth-place finish. Ranked ninth, India plays Olympic silver medallist China on August 16, then South Africa and higher-ranked England. It will target a better position than 2022’s ninth before switching focus to the Asian Games. For the first time, the World Cup for both genders involving 32 teams altogether, with a new and tricky format, is co-hosted by Belgium and the Netherlands. Both the Indian teams must play as cohesive units to build towards Los Angeles 2028.

stories.headline: Table Tennis federation challenges govt suspension, cites Olympic Charter autonomy
stories.deck: The federation also requested the ministry to keep its August 12 order in abeyance and review the matter.
stories.bodyText:
The Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI) on Thursday asked the Sports Ministry to reconsider its decision to suspend the federation's recognition, saying the move could affect the body's autonomy under the Olympic Charter.
The federation also requested the ministry to keep its August 12 order in abeyance and review the matter.
The Sports Ministry on Wednesday withdrew recognition of the TTFI and asked the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) to form an ad-hoc committee to administer table tennis in India. The Ministry cited governance issues, including the federation's failure to hold elections on time, after receiving an "unsatisfactory response" to a show-cause notice issued earlier this year.
In a statement issued by TTFI president Meghna Ahlawat, the federation said external or interim administration could have implications for the autonomy of a National Sports Federation.
"TTFI respectfully seeks the Ministry's kind consideration of the implications that any external or interim administrative arrangement may have in this regard, including the principles of autonomy recognised under Rules 27 and 28 of the Olympic Charter," TTFI said.
"The Olympic Charter and the Statutes of the International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF) recognise and expressly protect the autonomy of National Sports Federations and require their governance and administration to remain free from any third-party interference," it added.
The TTFI said it respects the Sports Ministry and acknowledged its role, but maintained that its governance is governed by its own Constitution and the principles of sporting autonomy.
"TTFI is an autonomous society duly registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, and is governed by its Constitution and General Body. The Federation holds the Ministry in the highest regard and recognises its role."
"At the same time, TTFI respectfully submits that the governance and administration of an autonomous National Sports Federation are guided by its Constitution and the applicable principles of sporting autonomy and good governance," the statement said.
Ahlawat took charge as TTFI president in December 2022. She is the wife of Haryana MLA Dushyant Chautala, whose father Ajay Singh Chautala is a former TTFI president.
The federation has faced several issues in recent months. In January, it suspended its secretary general and former player Kamlesh Mehta over alleged financial irregularities. Mehta challenged the decision in the Delhi High Court, which later quashed his suspension.
The TTFI said the issues mentioned in the Ministry's order had already been addressed before the show-cause notice was issued in June. It said the factual position was submitted to the Ministry on July 7 and argued that the deficiencies cited by the Ministry were either "factually incorrect" or had been "remedied" before the notice was issued.

briefs.headline: India emerge overall champions in Commonwealth Fencing
briefs.deck: Indian fencers won 13 gold, eight silver and 14 bronze medals across the U-23 and senior competitions
briefs.bodyText:
India have emerged as the overall champions at the Commonwealth Fencing Championship, returning with 35 medals from the event held in Lagos, Nigeria.
Indian fencers won 13 gold, eight silver and 14 bronze medals across the U-23 and senior competitions.
The senior Indian fencers claimed five gold medals in six events on the fourth day of the competition, securing honours in men’s sabre, women’s sabre, men’s épée, women’s épée and women’s foil, as well as a silver in men’s foil.
The performance also helped India win the Wilkinson Sword Trophy, awarded by the Commonwealth Fencing Federation to the country with the best overall results.
Rajeev Mehta, secretary-general, Fencing Association of India, said in a statement: “Lifting the Commonwealth Overall Championship title for the first time is a testament to the talent, discipline, and hard work within Indian fencing.”

briefs.headline: Praggnanandhaa loses to Keymer
briefs.deck: The Indian ace who has been rolling the roost for quite sometime had to finally concede a defeat against Keymer who has been making ground for himself in the last one year
briefs.bodyText:
Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa went down fighting against Vincent Keymer of Germany in the clash of youth in the Sinquefield Cup, part of the Grand Chess tour, here on Thursday.
The Indian ace who has been rolling the roost for quite sometime had to finally concede a defeat against Keymer who has been making ground for himself in the last one year.
The defeat meant that Praggnanandhaa remained on 1.5 points after three rounds and saw him slip to joint fourth spot with six rounds still to come in the $475,000 prize money tournament.
The biggest victory of the day was claimed by Philippine's Wesley So who has now been representing the United States for many years. On the receiving end was none other than Fabiano Caruana of US who was outfoxed by his opponent.
Wesley So emerged as the first sole leader of the tournament following his second straight win on 2.5 points and he is now followed by Armenian turned American Levon Aronian and ever-reliable Maxime Vachier Lagrave of France.
Praggnanandhaa is next in the queue on 1.5 points alongside Caruana, Keymer and surprise addition Sevian Samuels of the United States.
Javokhir Sindarov of Uzbekistan, who is going to challenge D Gukesh in the world championship scheduled later this year is on one point along with Anish Giri of Holland while another dutchman Jorden Van Foreest is on the last spot in the 10-player 9-rounds event with just a half point in his bucket.
It was not an easy day for Praggnanandhaa as he might have expected following good results against Keymer. The opening was not a problem but the Indian blundered away his chances and eventually it was a checkmate on board, seldom seen in top level Grandmasters games.
The hero of the day was Wesley So who gave little away against Caruana and when it mattered took his chances to win perhaps his most coveted victory in recent times. For Wesley it was the crowing moment when Caruana resigned as it also added to his hopes of being one of the four players to qualify for the grand finale in the Grand chess tour.
Anish Giri lost to Sevian after a long drawn game that lasted over 100 moves and Vachier-Lagrave drew with Sindarov without much fuss. In the other game of the day Aronian kept himself in contention signing peace with Jorden Van Foreest.

briefs.headline: Morkel backs KL Rahul to play key role in India's Test series against Sri Lanka
briefs.deck: Rahul is the sole survivor from India’s 2017 touring side’s batting group, with Morkel highlighting his experience as a valuable asset for the team in Galle
briefs.bodyText:
India’s bowling coach Morne Morkel has backed wicketkeeper-batter KL Rahul to play an important role for India in the upcoming Test series against Sri Lanka, highlighting the batter’s experience and his ability to help the younger members of the squad adapt to the conditions.
India will play the first Test of the two-match series from August 15 at the Galle International Stadium.
Notably, Rahul is the sole survivor from India’s 2017 touring side’s batting group, with Morkel highlighting his experience as a valuable asset for the team in Galle.
Speaking to reporters during the pre-match press conference ahead of the Galle Test, Morkel praised Rahul’s recent batting and said his experience and communication will help the younger players prepare for the conditions in Sri Lanka. He added that India’s early arrival has allowed the players to work on their individual game plans and understand how to score on the Galle surface.
“KL, the last couple of years, the way he’s been leading up front with the batting has been exceptional, and that’s a sort of communication that we expect him to speak to the guys here in the preparation at the nets and about what to expect. But I think, our guys have learned a lot about their games individually over the last couple of months and that’s one of the reasons why we’ve come out here 10 days earlier to give the guys the best opportunity to prepare to work on their individual game plans and individual game plans, and yeah, just to figure out how they’re going to score on the surface here,” Morkel said.

briefs.headline: HOCKEY WORLD CUP | Indian women will aim for the podium but with tempered expectations
briefs.bodyText:
An experienced Indian women’s hockey team will head to the Netherlands and Belgium for the 16th edition of the women’s FIH World Cup, starting on Friday, with renewed confidence, yet with tempered expectations.
A World Cup participation usually ushers in a sense of hope and anticipation for a nation’s contingent. But India’s tournament history, recent performances and a strong pool of title contenders offers little optimism as the current side aims to improve on a best-ever fourth-place finish, achieved at the inaugural edition in 1974.
After an uncertain period at the start of the year, the return of a rejuvenated Sjoerd Marijne, who masterminded the team’s fourth-place finish in the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, has brought about improved results.
World Cup qualification was secured on home soil before producing a perfect run to clinch the FIH Nations Cup title to earn promotion back to the Pro League for next season.
For Marijne, however, the World Cup offers a platform to fine-tune the team’s plans and conditioning for a more significant goal on the horizon: the Asian Games, which begins three weeks after the tournament. Gold medal in Japan will seal a return to the Olympics, after its failure to qualify in 2024.
Ranked ninth in the world, India is presented with an ideal tune-up, with China (world no. 4) — the 2022 Asian Games champion and 2024 Olympics runner-up — drawn in the same first round group alongside England (7) and South Africa (18).
China beat India, under former head coach Harendra Singh, twice at the Asia Cup last year and will want to underline its own credentials for a world title by making an emphatic start in their opening encounter.
India will come to bank heavily on its experienced core. Goalkeeper Savita Punia, defenders Nikki Pradhan and Sushila Chanu, midfielders Salima Tete and Neha Goyal, and forward Navneet Kaur bring plenty of tournament know-how and ability on the big stage.
The goal-scoring form of Navneet in open play and from Penalty Corners will be vital to India’s slim chances of battling it out for a podium place rather than entering the classification round for places between 9 and 16.
Progression into the second round isn’t going to make things any easier. A potentially daunting match-up against co-host Netherlands and one of Australia / Chile / Japan awaits.
There is no bigger favourite for the title than the Dutch, who are the three-time defending champion, aiming to add a 10th world crown to their burgeoning legacy in the women’s game.

briefs.headline: “Winning it on home soil, for the country, is all I could ask for”: P.V. Sindhu | Interview
briefs.bodyText:
P.V. Sindhu is easily the face of Indian badminton, not only representing the nation valiantly on the court, but also advocating for its evolution and identity off it. After winning incredible accolades on the world stage, the 31-year-old is naturally excited to have the opportunity to bid to reclaim the top step of the Badminton World Championships – an event she won in Basel in 2019 – on home soil.
“Playing at home is always good and exciting; our athletes will get to see a lot of top-level players up close… so much to look forward to,” Sindhu told The Hindu.
She was 14 when India last hosted the coveted event, in Hyderabad, and has had the best view of how the sport has evolved, in terms of infrastructure and intent.
ALSO READ | Sindhu launches her Centre for Sports Excellence in Visakhapatnam
“It was a long time back. I was a small kid who used to come to the stadium every single day, running from here to there. When I look back, I wonder what I was even doing. But from then until now, badminton as a sport has evolved so much. The support has been amazing – from the governments at both levels, the sports authorities and other sponsors.”
The biggest change from then to now has been the access players now have to an elaborate support staff that handles different aspects of an athlete’s performance, development, and longevity.
“A player might win medals – that’s one thing, and yes, infrastructure and the sponsors and support systems matter. But there’s also the work behind the scenes by the coaches and support staff. When we’re injured or not able to give our best, it’s their job to get us back on court as fit as possible, so they deserve a lot of credit for taking us all to the next level.”
Sindhu’s 2019 World gold was a watershed moment for Indian badminton and for women’s sports overall. It catapulted the ace shuttler into a commercial brand to be reckoned with too, but the bigger changes, for her, have come in how she approaches the sport.
“The whole game style – the way one thinks – changes a lot. I am more experienced now. Back then, we were just playing, making mistakes, accepting it and moving on. Now, we are more mature about what needs to change and how to make those changes happen. Even injury management has changed, physically and mentally. The changing support also made a big difference. Sponsor support, even from government schemes like the Target Olympic Podium Scheme, ensured that whenever I needed anything, it was made available to me. So, it’s been a different journey altogether, from when I started to now.”
ALSO READ | Horizons much bigger for the present players: Gopi Chand
Sindhu made a commendable Worlds debut, at just 18, in the 2013 chapter, returning with a historic bronze. She went on to add another bronze (2014), two silvers (2017, 2018), and a gold to her kitty.
A quarterfinal exit in 2021 and 2025, a stress fracture-induced withdrawal in 2022, and a second-round exit in 2023 mean Sindhu’s trophy cabinet is left yearning for another valuable addition. No longer an underdog, and fresh from a historic win at the Japan Open recently, Sindhu will hope to snap that drought at home this time.
“Irrespective of the medal, I want to give my best and play my game. I’ve worked hard, so I want to put in all my effort into this tournament. If I do get a medal, I’ll be more than happy, because winning it on home soil, for the country, is all I could ask for.”
